strengths: Adapting to an unknown number of comparator switches is a well-motivated problem with an identifiable audience in adversarial bandits and online learning.
The logarithmic grid of base algorithms and the decomposition into master and base regret clearly expose the variance introduced by importance weighting.
The progression from fixed learning rates to adaptive rates and a log-barrier master is understandable. The paper appropriately acknowledges that optimal worst-case adaptation remains unresolved.
weaknesses: Required, central: Theorem 2's advertised dependence on K is not established. Algorithm 2 sets η=√(H/T), so Lemma 4's negative term is −E[ρ_T]√T/(40√H log T). Equation (17) incorrectly introduces an additional √K. Maximizing the correctly substituted expression yields an upper bound of order SK√T, up to logarithmic factors, rather than S√(KT). The tuning, proof, and resulting comparison with EXP3.S must be reconciled.

Required proof corrections: Equations (4) and (8) incorrectly bound a maximum over the clipped simplex by the clipping mass. For two arms with constant losses (0,1), the first maximum in (4) equals (1−β)T_s, not at most βT_s. A fixed comparator smoothed toward the best arm would support the intended argument. Lemma 2 also applies a pathwise OMD inequality to the true losses although the update uses estimated losses; the expectation argument needs to be stated correctly.

Required for implementation: Remark 1 does not generally implement the analyzed updates. Mixing an unconstrained solution with uniform mass differs from Bregman projection onto the clipped simplex. Moreover, its fixed-rate cumulative-loss formulas do not describe Algorithm 2's changing, coordinate-dependent learning rates. Provide updates consistent with the algorithms and proofs.

Required scope correction: Algorithm 1 can have an empty feasible domain because αH=(K/T)^(1/3)√H can exceed 1. The manuscript needs an applicable parameter restriction or a valid alternative initialization for this regime.

Required lower-bound correction: Section 2.1 uses Cauchy–Schwarz in the wrong direction: it upper-bounds the sum of square roots of segment lengths. Establish the minimax lower bound using an explicit hard construction with balanced segments, and include the linear-regret cap or restrict the parameter range.

Optional: An interpretable instance class or worked example controlling ρ_T(h†) would clarify when the conditional bound improves on the worst-case guarantee. Additional experiments or state-of-the-art performance are not necessary for this theoretical contribution.
